editions.text:
The station's busiest day in the past week recorded 142 feeder visits and 15 species, far exceeding the recent average of roughly 51 visits. Tufted Titmice dominated the visual log with 70 confident sightings, opening and closing the day's activity, while Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays led the auditory count. This activity level aligns with the addition of a new tube seed feeder installed on the left hook of the pole earlier in the week.

The 06:52 switch to the new microphone source captures the station's full auditory range, including first-time detections for Carolina Chickadees, House Finches, Northern Mockingbirds, and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds. These species were already known to the area but had not been reliably identified by the previous audio system. The new source also records the first confident visual sightings of Gray Catbirds and House Finches at this station.

Regulars such as Carolina Wrens, Eastern Towhees, and American Crows held steady throughout the day, with Crows showing a noticeable increase in evening activity. No new station changes occurred after the morning audio upgrade and the afternoon seed feeder replacement.

The morning began with a Blue Jay perched on the ground near the nectar source thirteen minutes after sunrise, immediately followed by a Tufted Titmouse taking the tube feeder at 07:38. Carolina Wrens called constantly.

Total visits reached 159 across 16 species, compared to the typical 39 at this hour. Tufted Titmice recorded 64 confident visits, while Carolina Chickadees contributed 46. Carolina Wrens registered 160 detections and Northern Cardinals 48, exceeding the recent daily average of 87 sounds. Eastern Towhees and Northern Mockingbirds also registered.
